brief: Make this batch Kaspa-centric: there is a lot of Kaspa content in this stream, so the tweets, threads, polls, quizzes and YT/IG posts should lean on the Kaspa topics first (KCC20 / Nacho migration deadline January 31, Kaspa chart vs early Bitcoin, Kaspa's first bear market vs Bitcoin's 50 week MA, the 3.33 dollar target, GHOSTDAG / blockDAG, Bitcoin maxis rotating to Kaspa, the Kaspa conference cruise).

fact_check.claim: 'the four-year cycle zombies still have a day left... 25 hours to prove me wrong to get a new bottom... 40K Bitcoin in October' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified and updated to the close: October 2026 closed around $77.3K to $77.6K, down about 7% (reported as the worst October since 2014); the October low was about $76.2K while the 2026 low remains July's ~$58.6K, so no October bottom printed. Copy: 'October closed down 7%, the worst October since 2014, and the 2026 low is still July's $58K.'
fact_check.source: financefeeds.com (Oct close $77,582, open $83,624, low $76,326); cryptoticker.io; cryptonews.net ('worst October finish since 2014'); CoinGecko daily history (2026 monthly lows, July low $58,566), pulled 2026-11-02

fact_check.claim: 'Bitcoin is still above the 50-week moving average... two weekly closes below is a bear market' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified: on Kraken XBTUSD weekly candles Bitcoin closed below its 50-week SMA from the week of Nov 6 2025 until it reclaimed in the week of Sept 17 2026 (close $84,385 vs SMA $78,606) and has stayed above since; the week ending Oct 29 closed $77,672 vs SMA $75,924, low $76,156 (above). CoinGecko Sunday closes agree (Nov 1: $77,521 vs SMA $75,706). Copy says 'closed the month above its 50-week SMA' (a past fact) rather than a live level.
fact_check.source: api.kraken.com OHLC XBTUSD interval=10080 and api.coingecko.com bitcoin market_chart (365d), computed 2026-11-02

fact_check.claim: 'Binance got a hack for $5.6 billion dollars, the largest heist in human history... Bitcoin only went down 6.8%' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified in substance, numbers updated: the Oct 29 2026 Binance hack is reported at about $6.3 billion (Chainalysis ~$5.9B at the time; Binance set aside $6.34B), the largest crypto theft on record; Bitcoin fell roughly 3% to 5% over 24 hours to a six-week low near $76.4K to $77K. Copy: '$6.3 billion drained from Binance on October 29... $BTC dropped about 5%'. 'Largest heist in human history' is softened to 'biggest heist in crypto history'.
fact_check.source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Binance_hack; cnn.com 2026/10/30; aljazeera.com 2026/10/30; coindesk.com 2026/10/29; e27.co (4.87% drop); blockchainreporter.net (~4%); stocktwits/CoinGlass (>3%)

fact_check.claim: 'Nacho Migration is live, KCC-20 is live in Kaspa L1... Migration deadline January 31st, after this date un-migrated tokens will not be eligible... you got to bridge over' (transcript, Mike reading Nacho the Kat's post on stream)
fact_check.verdict: verified: the NACHO move to KCC-20 opened on mainnet October 30 2026, one way, 1:1, from KRC-20, Igra L2 or Kasplex L2, and the window closes January 31 2027 (KuCoin repost of the @KASPAglobal post). The 'not eligible after' consequence is the line Mike read aloud from the post. 'KCC-20 is live' rides on the Oct 21 Final declaration (prior ledger). A GitHub community report dated Oct 29 said no migration path was live yet, which predates the Oct 30 opening. Copy avoids calling Nacho 'the first' KRC-20 to migrate in tweets; the IG caption says 'one of the first big KRC-20 names'.
fact_check.source: kucoin.com/news/insight/KAS/6ae5dda4bbcb520007454e85 (Oct 31); crypto.news kaspa-finalizes-kcc-native-token-app-standards (Oct 21); news.bitcoin.com Kasplex indexer article (Sept 20 exploit); github.com/neoalphavault-png/kaspa-pulse/pull/217

fact_check.claim: 'a third-party indexer... got exploited' / KRC-20 indexer context (drafted copy)
fact_check.verdict: verified: on September 20 2026 an attacker used a signature-bypass flaw in the Kasplex KRC-20 indexer to credit forged transfers and drain two token pools; the team says the flaw was in the indexer, not in Kaspa. KCC-20 puts token rules into covenants that L1 consensus checks.

fact_check.claim: 'Bitcoin had Miami, Ethereum had Devcon, now it's Kaspa's turn... four-day experience... investing up to a million in Kaspa startups... Port of Miami, April 9th through the 12th, 2027... Norwegian Cruise Line, four days three nights' (transcript, promo video played on stream)
fact_check.verdict: verified: KaspaBots announced the Kaspa Conference on Oct 28 2026 for April 9-12 2027, Miami, Florida, aboard a Norwegian Cruise Line ship; virtual access $97 early bird (regularly $197) until December 31 2026; KaspaBots says up to $1M will go into $KAS startups, 'four days of builders, investors and community'. NOT verified and dropped: 'all ticket proceeds supporting Kaspa core', the accelerator / 'Kaspa University' / demo-day structure, and the 'I used to be a Bitcoin maxi' testimonial line. Copy: 'four-day cruise out of Miami, April 9 to 12, 2027, with up to $1 million going into Kaspa startups'.

fact_check.claim: Viewer's overlay: 'two different cryptos... 11 years apart identical bear market along with identical current price action before the full bull market' / 'Kaspa's bear market is identical to Bitcoin's first real bear market' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified in the general form and quantified: Bitcoin's first real bear ran from the December 2013 top (~$1,127 to $1,150) to the January 2015 low (~$152 to $175), an 84% to 86% drawdown over about 13 months, and BTC was back at new all-time highs by early 2017 (about two years after the low). Kaspa's first bear ran from the July 31 2024 ATH ($0.2074) to the August 14 2026 low ($0.02526), an 88% drawdown. 'Identical' is written as 'same shape'; '11 years apart' holds for the two lows (Jan 2015 vs Aug 2026).
fact_check.source: nasdaq.com Bitcoin Bear Markets; bitcoinmagazine.com (84.82%); fxempire PrimeXBT research (86%); api.coingecko.com kaspa (ATH, 365d daily history), pulled 2026-11-02

fact_check.claim: 'Kaspa was not in a bear market in 2022... Kaspa goes into a bear market in December of 2024... stays nearly two years, right up until September, and now it's above its 50-week moving average' (transcript, Mike's chart)
fact_check.verdict: verified on Kraken weekly candles for the 2026 part: KAS closed above its 50-week SMA in the week of Sept 17 2026 (0.0385 vs 0.0370) for six consecutive weekly closes through Oct 22, and the week that began Oct 29 is trading below it (0.0324 vs 0.0356) after the Binance flush; Bitcoin reclaimed its own 50-week SMA in the same week (Sept 17). The December 2024 cross cannot be computed from Kraken (KAS listed Nov 2024) and is written as Mike's own chart read ('on my chart'); it is consistent with the Kraken closes falling from $0.164 to $0.117 across December 2024 against a 2024 average price near $0.15. Kaspa's 2022 bull run (from under a cent to $0.01+ while BTC fell) is public price history. Copy states the retest honestly: 'Six weekly closes above, then the Binance flush dragged it back to the line this week.'
fact_check.source: api.kraken.com OHLC KASUSD interval=10080 (103 weeks) and XBTUSD, computed 2026-11-02; api.coingecko.com kaspa market_chart 365d

fact_check.claim: 'A $3 Kaspa is only $100 billion market cap... if there is $100 trillion market cap with crypto... $3 is kind of bearish' / '$3.33, that would be a nice target, I get my yacht' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: updated to real supply: Kaspa circulating supply is 27.79 billion KAS, so $3 is about $83 billion and $3.33 about $93 billion (the transcript's '$100 billion' is corrected everywhere). Current KAS price $0.0325 (3.2 cents), market cap about $903 million, 84% under the ATH. Total crypto market cap is about $2.59 trillion. The $100 trillion figure is Mike's thesis and is written as his view.

fact_check.claim: 'Yonatan tried making [improvements] for BTC that were shot down... GHOSTDAG was his proposal, he turned it into a graph' / 'greediest heaviest observed subtree... in the Ethereum white paper' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified in the general form: Sompolinsky and Zohar's 2013 paper (IACR ePrint 2013/881, published as 'Secure High-Rate Transaction Processing in Bitcoin', FC 2015) proposed the GHOST rule as a modification to how Bitcoin nodes build the chain; Bitcoin did not adopt it, Ethereum implemented a variant early on, and the PHANTOM/GHOSTDAG paper (Sompolinsky, Wyborski, Zohar) generalizes Nakamoto consensus to a DAG of blocks, implemented as Kaspa. 'Shot down' is written as 'Bitcoin never adopted it'; the Ethereum link is written as 'built a variant of it into its early design', not as a whitepaper citation claim.

fact_check.claim: 'Kaspa is a 12-lane highway... blocks working in 12 lanes... one lane fans out into multiple lanes and then converges' (transcript, viewer analogy + Mike)
fact_check.verdict: kept as a viewer's analogy, attributed ('one of my viewers put it best'); the technical anchor is verified: Kaspa runs 10 blocks per second since the Crescendo hard fork activated on mainnet May 5 2025.

fact_check.claim: 'there's going to be a day where a lot of Bitcoin maxis move over to Kaspa... Michael Saylor types... Winklevoss twins... eventually Ethereum is going to overtake Bitcoin' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: Mike's thesis (persona core_theses: ETH flips BTC, maxis seek a PoW alt, they find KAS), written in first person as a theory. The speculation that named figures (Saylor, Winklevoss) are quietly stacking Kaspa is unverifiable and is NOT used anywhere; no named person appears in copy or imagery.
fact_check.source: persona/persona.json core_theses; no external claim made

Kaspa's chart looks just like early Bitcoin. Not the vibes, the actual structure: the first real bear market, the drawdown, the reclaim. One of you dropped the overlay in my stream this week and I have been staring at it since. Here is what lines up, and the one thing about Kaspa's bear market that I had never thought about.

Start with Bitcoin's first real bear. From the December 2013 top near $1,150 to the January 2015 low near $170 is an 85% drawdown over about 13 months. Then two years of base building, and by early 2017 $BTC was printing new all-time highs.

Now Kaspa. From the July 2024 top at 20.7 cents to the August 2026 low at 2.5 cents is an 88% drawdown. Eleven years apart, same shape: a parabolic first run, a long grinding first bear, and a bottom that nobody rings a bell for.

Here is the part I had never considered until this week. Kaspa never had a 2022 bear market. In crypto the common definition of a bear market is weekly closes under the 50-week SMA, and Bitcoin spent most of 2022 under that line. Kaspa did not. It was in its first bull run the entire time. On my chart Kaspa only lost its 50-week SMA in December 2024, so its first bear market started then and ran almost two years.

And in September it closed back above that line. Kaspa reclaimed its 50-week SMA for the first time since December 2024, in the same week Bitcoin reclaimed its own. It held the line for six weekly closes. Then the Binance hack flushed the whole market, $6.3 billion drained in the biggest heist in crypto history, and $KAS slipped back to the line. It sits at 3.2 cents, 84% under its high, while Bitcoin is still above its 50-week SMA.

So that is the setup: a first bear market with Bitcoin's 2015 shape, a reclaim that is being retested, and a market cap under a billion dollars. A $3 Kaspa is an $83 billion market cap. If crypto grows into the $100 trillion asset class I think it becomes, that number is low, not high. My $3.33 target gets me the yacht; it might also be conservative. Never financial advice.

yt_posts.topic: Bitcoin maxis will end up in Kaspa: the GHOST to GHOSTDAG lineage, the blockDAG highway, the ETH-flips-BTC cascade, the Kaspa Conference cruise, the Nacho migration
yt_posts.body_style: hook-and-thesis-first argument chain: the lineage, the mechanics, the cascade, the ecosystem signals, the price
yt_posts.body:
Bitcoin maxis are going to end up in Kaspa. Not all of them, and not this year, but the path is already drawn, and the first clue is sitting in a 2013 research paper written for Bitcoin itself. Here is the whole cascade.

Start with where Kaspa comes from. In 2013 Yonatan Sompolinsky and Aviv Zohar published GHOST, a paper literally titled Secure High-Rate Transaction Processing in Bitcoin. It was a fix for Bitcoin's scaling problem: stop throwing away the blocks that arrive at the same time and use them. Bitcoin never adopted it. Ethereum built a variant of it into its early design. Then Sompolinsky generalized the idea into GHOSTDAG, and Kaspa is the full implementation: a proof-of-work blockDAG running 10 blocks per second since the Crescendo hard fork in May 2025.

One of my viewers put it best this week: Kaspa is a 12-lane highway. A chain is one lane and every block waits its turn. A blockDAG fans one lane out into many parallel lanes and then merges them back together in order. Same proof of work, same fair launch with no premine, just the part of the Bitcoin design that was left on the table in 2013.

Now the cascade. My theory is that Ethereum eventually knocks Bitcoin out of the number one spot, and the way $ETH has been trading I am more convinced, not less. When that happens, the Bitcoin maxis who care about proof of work and fair launch go looking for the next thing, and there is exactly one chain built on those principles with a research lineage straight back to Bitcoin. Some move the first year, more the next. A slow cascade, not a flip of a switch.

The ecosystem is already acting like it. This week KaspaBots announced the Kaspa Conference: four days aboard a Norwegian Cruise Line ship out of Miami, April 9 to 12, 2027, with up to $1 million going into Kaspa startups. Bitcoin had Miami. Ethereum had Devcon. Kaspa gets a ship. And on the token side, Nacho the Kat opened its migration to KCC-20 on the Kaspa L1 on October 30, with the window closing January 31, 2027: token rules enforced by Kaspa consensus, not by a third-party indexer.

$KAS is 3.2 cents, 84% under its high, with a market cap under a billion dollars. That is the entry the maxis will wish they took. Never financial advice.

So tell me in the comments: when do the Bitcoin maxis move? Already happening quietly, when ETH flips BTC, after a new Kaspa all-time high, or never? And if you were a maxi who came over, what flipped you?
